declared_differences.why: the `error` object of every tool error carries four fields of this engine (code, stage, retryable, details) beside the reference's

the smali text follows baksmali's writing (p-registers for parameters, :cond_N/:goto_N/:try_start_N labels, .catch lines beside the code, an L on wide literals, a backslash before an apostrophe in strings); the reference writes v-registers, :label_XXXX, .catch lines at the end, no L, a bare apostrophe. The two texts are reduced to the same form (canon_smali) and must be equal: instructions, operands, literals, branch targets, payloads and exception tables. The numbers that depend on the length of the text (total_bytes, total_lines, start_line, end_line, next_offset, the mid-line flags) are compared only when the text is identical.
an error's `message` is this server's own words. Its `kind` (through KIND_ALIASES) and the file_id, method_idx and code_unit_offset it echoes are compared.

an argument of the wrong type, an unknown field, or a value outside its range (limit, max_lines, method_limit, timeout_ms) is a JSON-RPC invalid-params error here; the reference answers a tool result with isError (the serde message, or kind invalid_input).

the reference refuses max_bytes outside 4096..=131072 and timeout_ms outside 1..=60000, and `mode: null` for get_manifest; this server's max_bytes is a budget the answer must fit in (over it: quota_exceeded) and it takes `null` as the default.

a method whose invoke names a different number of registers than its prototype takes is rendered as the bytes say (the invoke is visible and wrong); the reference refuses the whole method (invalid_input, with the offset of the invoke). Showing the code of a damaged or obfuscated method is the more useful answer.
the summary mode here also names the method's `declaration`.
the xml mode of get_manifest (MDD-072) is refused as `not_implemented`; it is not compared.
every decode answer that shows text names the version of its text (`text_format`); a context row also gives `source_total_lines`, the line count of the full text its `line N:` numbers index.

a class page also carries `class`: the class's own facts (flags, superclass, source file, interfaces, field counts) and, in the text modes on the first page, its declaration, fields and annotations as a text; and a method row may carry `omitted`, what its text leaves out. The reference has neither.

the smali text here also carries annotation blocks, `.param` lines and debug directives (`.line`, `.local`, `.end local`, `.restart local`, `.prologue`, `.epilogue`, `.source`) that the reference never writes; canon_smali drops them before the texts are compared, so the instructions, operands, targets, payloads and exception tables are what is compared.

the context view keeps the same kinds of lines as the reference's (method line, registers line, label lines, catch lines; checked against the reference for every method of the fixture). Its `line N:` numbers count the lines of this server's own full text, so they are compared only through canon_context, which drops the numbers and merges the labels that name one address; the labels themselves are named by baksmali's conventions here.

in a class page `max_bytes` is one budget of UTF-8 bytes for the text of all its methods (the reference's counts the serialized answer, twice); a class page's answer is compared only where no budget is asked for.
list_tables names the 17 HostLab contract relations (as objects with name, kind and column_count) where the reference lists 56 names; list_datasets reports this server's own limits.

when a request is wrong in several ways, both engines refuse it, but the reference names the dataset first, then timeout_ms, max_bytes and the rest, and this server checks the schema of the arguments before it looks for the dataset.
a 1 ms deadline: the reference ran out of time; whether this server does depends on the clock.

residual: the reference writes no annotation, parameter name, debug directive, class header or field line: those parts of mdd.smali.v1 have no reference output to equal; they are checked against an independent reader of the bytes and hand-written texts, and the reference replay removes them (EXTRA DIRECTIVES) before it compares instructions

a parameter's annotations are placed only when the method's slots are as many as its prototype's parameters; otherwise they are counted in omitted
